name: 8-Bit Arcade
summary: A late NES cartridge: strict 2C02 palette, black-outlined sprites posed from parts, 8-frame walks and tile-language meadows.
description: Looks like it came from a late-era NES/Famicom cartridge. Every colour comes from the NES PPU palette, every sprite part has at most three colours plus a 1-px black outline, and the world is built from flat colour areas with hard tile-style edges: a dark-green meadow whose tufts gather along the edges, brown forest floor behind black cliff lines with a dithered canopy-shade band, ochre roads with wheel ruts, navy ponds ringed with cattails and grey brick plazas with tombstones. Figures are posed from parts and animate in held frames: an 8-frame walk with counter-swinging arms and a head that lands a frame late, hopping beets that squash and stretch, ghosts that unroll in checker pixels. There is no anti-aliasing, gradient or alpha in the world; transparency is a checkerboard and blinking is sprite flicker.
avoidFor: designs needing subtle lighting or many similar figure types

difficulty.why: Assets are small char grids with at most 3 colours per part plus an automatic black outline, but figures are posed from part tables (legs, arms, head, crown), so every cycle needs 4–8 thought-through poses with a lagging feature; the strict NES palette keeps colour decisions easy.

technique.resolution: 1 art pixel = 1.5 world units, so the 360-unit-tall view is a 240-row art buffer (NES height). Display scale up = max(1, round(screenH / 240)), buffer = ceil(screen / up), nearest-neighbour upscale. Ground chunks of 256 world units bake at 171 × 171 px.
technique.summary: Sprites are char grids mapped to NES colours by a builder that adds a 1-px black outline; figures are composed from posed parts (legs table, sleeve/hand table, head, scarf or leaf crown) and baked lazily per pose. The ground is a material map on a 2×2-pixel block grid with tile-language edge rules, a canopy dither band, wheel ruts and clustered glyph decals.
technique.linework: 1-px pure black #000000 outline around every sprite, generated from the 4-neighbourhood of filled pixels (8-neighbour for number digits). Ground boundaries are single 1-px lines: black between grass and forest/water/plaza, light-green #00A800 lip on grass, ochre lip on forest, dark-brown edge on roads, sand lip where road meets water.
technique.shading: Flat colour fills. Volume comes from one light and one dark accent per part (canopy: light #58D854 crescent upper left, black arc lower right; pumpkin head: #FCA044 glint, #881400 ribs and underside; bulbs: #F878F8 highlight), black far limbs for depth and checkerboard dithering of black for shade. No gradients, no blending.
technique.lighting: No light system. The world is evenly lit; the only 'lighting' is the lantern sprite blinking between gold #F8B800 and white glass at 4 Hz and white-hot burst cores.
technique.texture: No noise texture. Surfaces get NES tile decals instead: 2-row grass tufts on an 8-px grid, 3×3 flowers, 1–2 px red/ochre leaf litter and black twigs on forest floor, pebbles on roads, a 12 × 6 running-bond brick tile on plazas, 2-frame animated wave glyphs on water.

paletteRules: Only colours from the NES 2C02 master palette; no tints, no mixes, no alpha in the world.

Each sprite part uses at most 3 colours plus the black outline; the main character is stacked from parts (head orange/dark red/light-orange glint, yellow face glow, green stem and scarf, blue/navy/cream tunic, brown belt and boots) and its far limbs are black.
Ground is roughly 50% #005800 green, 25% #503000 forest floor, 10% #AC7C00 road, the rest water/stone/decals.
Creature variants are designed: the purple beet and the crimson radish share a builder but differ in bulb proportions, crown shape and palette; ghosts are white with cyan shade.

Flash is a palette swap, never an overlay: white body with a red outline and face for root creatures and the large creature, yellow/red for ghosts, alternating all-white and all-red for the main character.
Pure black is reserved for outlines, cliff lines, shadows and UI windows.

typography.role: Everything: HUD labels, numbers, menus, cards
typography.css: font: 16px/1 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #fcfcfc; text-shadow: none; letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: uppercase;

world.summary: A top-down overworld made of five flat materials (grass, forest floor, road, water, stone plaza) classified on a 2×2-art-pixel block grid from noise fields, outlined with NES tile edge rules, given a dithered canopy-shade band inside forests and wheel ruts on roads, then stamped with clustered glyph decals: tufts line every edge, flowers grow in small beds, the open meadow stays calm.
layers: Material map per 2×2 px block: plaza (octagon rect) > water (warped noise < 0.335) > road (distance to two noise-curve roads < 11 units) > forest (warped noise > 0.555) > grass
Base fills: grass #005800, forest #503000, road #AC7C00, water #0000BC, plaza brick tile #7C7C7C/#BCBCBC/#000000

Edge pixels: grass lip #00A800, black cliff forest/grass, ochre forest lip vs road/water, dark-brown road edge, sand road lip vs water, black + blue ring around water, black + light-grey ring around plazas
Per frame: 2-frame wave glyphs (cyan or blue, 5×2 px) toggling at 2.2 Hz on water anchors
Canopy shade: black checker pixels inside the forest within 2 px of grass (sparser at 3 px), so forests read as a raised, shaded mass
Wheel ruts: #503000 pixels where the road-centre distance is 5.4 ± 0.6 units, broken on ~1 in 7 hashed 8-px cells
Clustered decals: tufts within 5 px of other materials (70 %) and in fbm patches, 1.8 % on open meadow; flower beds of 3–6 heads on a 23-px grid; clumped leaf litter; pebbles only on road shoulders

characters.summary: Figures are posed from parts on char grids and baked per pose. Main character (16 × 20 grid, ~18 × 27 units of body): a round orange #E45C10 pumpkin head with #881400 ribs, a #FCA044 glint and a carved #F8D878 face, a curled stem with a leaf, a green scarf with a trailing tail, a #0078F8 tunic with brown belt and cream buckle, navy trousers, brown boots, black far limbs. Small creatures (15 × 18): a purple beet with a three-leaf fan crown and a crimson radish with two curling leaves, angry brows and a toothy grin, hopping on root legs. Fast creature: a white hooded ghost with solid black eyes, a reaching arm and a waving checker tail. Large creature (28 × 34): a beet-headed burlap sack golem with gold eyes, a stitched grin, swinging root arms and stumpy legs.
rules: Every part ≤ 3 colours + the automatic 1-px black outline; far arm and far leg are black for depth; facing = horizontal flip

Main character walk: 8 computed poses (contact, down, passing, up × 2) with body offsets [0,1,0,-1,…], counter-swinging arms, the head using the previous frame's offset (lands late), scarf flapping a frame behind
Idle: breath every 1.1 s with the head following 0.12 s later, leaf flick, blink every 3.4 s, scarf flutter every 4.3 s; every figure has its own phase offset

Dash: 50 ms crouch wind-up → split stretch pose with two checker afterimages → 120 ms skid; throw arm snaps out for 90 ms after a shot; hurt = recoil pose in alternating white/red palettes, then flicker
Small creatures hop in 4 frames: squash 6.3 × 8 → push → stretch 4.7 × 10 (2 px up) → fall; the leaf crown lags (droops going up, lifts falling)
Ghost: 4 tail frames at 7 fps, eased lift [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1] at 5 fps, reaching arm, mouth opening every 2.6 s
Large creature: 4-frame stomp with a 1-px body drop and dust on each contact, arms swinging opposite to the legs
Hit ~130 ms: squash pose + shut eyes + 2-px recoil + flash palette; appear: dirt mound heaves → climb-out clip → land (ghosts unroll in checker); disappear: 100 ms white/red pop → 4-frame burst

props.summary: Outlined NES sprites standing on the ground, built with the same grid builder: circle-built round trees (24 × 28, green or 16 % autumn), tiered pines (17 × 31) in forest interiors, bushes, cattail stands at pond shores, grey dead trees, rocks, orange pumpkins, ochre fences and signposts, white tombstones and a stone pumpkin statue on brick plazas.
rules: Same rules as figures: 1-px black outline, max 3 colours + black, flat fills, feet anchor on whole art pixels, y-sorted with the figures
Tree and bush canopies are overlapping circles: black lower-right rim (dd > 0.72 && nx + ny > 0.45), light upper-left crescent, global checker shade over the lower right
Trees: #00A800 canopy with #58D854 highlight (autumn: #AC7C00 with #F8D878) over a dark-red #881400 trunk with a black right edge
Every tree has a see-through checker copy (checker: 0) drawn when a figure stands behind it
Stone props (rocks, dead trees, tombstones, statue) use white/light grey on the upper left and mid grey on the right; tombstones carry a black cross
Wood props (fences, signposts) are ochre #AC7C00 with dark-brown #503000 rails and lines
Only trees (20 px), dead trees (12 px) and the statue (16 px) cast checker shadows

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: 3 frames over 0.2 s: 7 × 7 white cross flash → 9 × 9 gold/red X of sparks around a white core → four far gold corner dots; plus 3 debris bits in the struck figure's colours (gravity 170).

effects.name: Disappear sequence
effects.how: The figure's own white pop with a red outline in its squash pose (~100 ms), then 4 procedural burst frames on a (ceil(18R)|1)² grid: white core + gold cross, white/gold disc with red rays, red/gold checker ring, 8 flying bits. R = 1 or 1.7. Ghosts instead lose rows from the bottom while rising 14 px.

effects.name: Debris and residue
effects.how: 6–12 chunks in the figure's colours (2-px chunks get a black 1-px rim like sprites, gravity 230), tumbling 2 × 2 leaf scraps from root creatures, rising cyan stars from ghosts; a small smoke puff lingers 0.6–0.8 s and flickers out.

effects.name: Appear sequence
effects.how: A 12-px (20-px for the large creature) ochre/brown dirt mound heaves for 0.16 s, the creature climbs out (only its top rows drawn, the mound covers the cut) and lands in its squash frame; ghosts unroll from the hood down in flickering checker pixels.

effects.name: Checker transparency
effects.how: Ghost tails, afterimages and see-through trees drop every other pixel ((x + y + parity) & 1); parity flips every 2 frames so tails shimmer like NES sprite multiplexing.

effects.name: Collect ring
effects.how: An expanding diamond outline (radius 3, 5, 7) in cyan or gold, a rising star and 3 pixels thrown upwards.

effects.name: Light column
effects.how: A 9 × 40 px checker pillar (white core, gold sides, 2 parities alternating every 4 frames) that shrinks from the top over 0.55 s, with a gold ring and 10 outward stars.

effects.name: Collectibles and lantern
effects.how: Cyan 5 × 6 and gold 7 × 8 diamonds spin through 4 frames, bob [0,1,2,1] and flash a star glint every ~1.8 s; the 9 × 12 orbiting lantern flickers gold → yellow → white in the sequence 0,1,0,2,1,0 at 9 fps with a trailing gold spark.

atmosphere.summary: No light system, no post-processing in the world: even flat light with highlights baked into sprites, checker-dithered black shadows locked to the screen grid, checkerboard transparency, flicker for blinking, and only faint display scanlines when the upscale is 3 or more.
rules: Shadows are black ellipses w × round(w/3) with only checker pixels set; two parities baked, the one matching (screenX + screenY) & 1 is used
Shadow sizes: 8 ghost, 12 main character / small creature / dead tree, 16 statue, 20 tree, 24 large creature; all shadows drawn before any sprite
Light is implied only by upper-left sprite highlights and blinking glows (lantern glass gold/white at 4 Hz, white burst cores)
Transparency is always a checkerboard, never alpha; fading = flicker (skip drawing when frameCounter & 2)
No vignette, no fog, no bloom, no colour grading
Display-only CRT hint when up >= 3: darken the last display row of every art row with rgba(0,0,0,0.16) — the only alpha in the style
Menus dim the world with a black checker dither, never a translucent overlay; the black HUD bar frames the top of the screen

ui.summary: A solid black NES status bar across the top: red uppercase labels (-LIFE-), a row of 8 × 7 px hearts at 3×, a big white clock with a red caption, a counter with a tiny creature icon, a segmented cyan/blue progress bar with a 4-px white frame. Menus and cards are black windows with double white borders and a blinking triangle cursor; overlay screens dim the world with a black checker dither.

motion: Held poses on the NES beat (8–12 fps): main character walk = floor(anim × 1.3) & 7 over 8 poses (~0.67 s cycle), small creatures floor(anim × 2.2 + phase) & 3, large creature floor(anim × 1.6 + phase) & 3.

Follow-through: the main character's head uses the previous frame's body offset, the scarf flaps one frame behind, the stem leaf lifts when the head drops; beet crowns droop going up and lift falling; ghost tails wave through 4 frames.
Idle life on varied timers with a per-figure phase: breath 1.1 s, blink 3.4 s, leaf 1.5 fps, scarf flutter 4.3 s; ghosts float on the eased lift [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1] at 5 fps.
States: dash wind-up 50 ms → stretch → skid 120 ms; hit ~130 ms squash + flash + recoil; appear 0.45 s mound → climb → land; disappear 0.35 s pop → burst.
Collectibles spin 0,0,0,1,2,3 at 9 fps and bob [0,1,2,1] at 4 fps; lanterns flicker 0,1,0,2,1,0 at 9 fps.
No easing and no sub-pixel motion: positions round to whole art pixels; CSS transitions are none and blinks use steps(1).
Blinking flicker: skip drawing when (frameCounter & 2); fading particles and numbers blink the same way. Water waves toggle at 2.2 Hz.
do: Build figures from posed parts on a char grid (legs table, sleeve/hand table, head, scarf or crown) and bake each pose once.
Keep each sprite part to 3 colours + black from the NES palette list; make far limbs black for depth.
Animate with real held poses: 8-frame walks, 4-frame squash & stretch hops and stomps, a head or crown that lands a frame late, per-figure phase offsets.
Give every state its own sequence: wind-up before a dash, squash on hit, a dirt mound before an appearance, a white pop before a burst.
Cluster ground decals along edges and in patches; leave open meadow calm.
Snap every blit to whole art pixels and upscale with smoothing off; use checkerboard pixels for transparency and flicker for blinking.
Use Press Start 2P at multiples of 8 px for all text, with uppercase red labels.
dont: No gradients, glows, blur, alpha fades or anti-aliased shapes in the world.
No colours outside the NES palette (no #333 greys, no pastel tints).
No coloured or 2-px outlines on figures (the red outline of the hit flash is the only exception).
No rotation or scaling of sprites — use extra poses or flips instead.
No 2-frame leg toggles or plain sine bobs, and no crowds sharing one animation phase.
No evenly sprinkled tufts, pebbles or leaves over a whole material; no noise textures on the ground.
No smooth tweened UI: no rounded corners, no drop-shadow blur, no transitions.
performance: Cheap. Sprites are tiny canvases baked once per pose into a Map (walk, hop, float and stomp poses are warmed at init, rare poses bake on first use in well under a millisecond); effect frames and shadows are baked at init; floating numbers are cached per value. Ground chunks (171 × 171 px) bake incrementally in a generator that samples the noise fields on an 8-px grid, stores the road distance per pixel for ruts and checks decal neighbours inside a 14-px margin so stamps stay seamless. Per frame only drawImage blits (some with a source rect for climb-out and dissolve clips), a few wave fillRects and an optional scanline pattern.
